answer: Passport chip binding: the operator taps an e-passport on a phone, and the validator reads the chip data signed by the issuing country, checks that signature against the published country certificate list, and stores only a salted hash of the document number. A farm cannot wander from name to name on one document; reaching the summit of a thousand identities needs a thousand genuine passports, each with fees and an in-person application. Limitation: stolen or fraudulently issued passports slip through, and people without one, like some remote island residents, are excluded.
